newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France to fly more summer cargo hours.
newsitem.headline: Air France to fly more summer cargo hours.

text.p: Air France Cargo said 35,000 flying hours were planned for its Boeing 747-200F fleet during the 1997 summer season which runs from end-March to end-October, a rise of 14 percent on the same period last year.
The carrier's freighter fleet is set rise to 12 aircraft at the end of this month with the arrival of an additional 747-200F, which has been converted from passenger/cargo combi configuration.

As part of its summer 1997 freighter programme, Air France said it was launching a new weekly 747-200F cargo service between Paris and West Africa, the full routeing reading: Paris-Cotonou (Benin)-Libreville (Gabon)-Paris.
Air France already serves Cotonou with a twice-weekly Boeing 747-200 combi service and Brazzaville (Congo) with a three-times weekly passenger service using a 747-400 combis and Airbus A310-300s.

"The freighter service will fully compensate for the loss of cargo capacity to these destinations as a result of the withdrawal of 747-200 combis on passenger services," an Air France Cargo official told Reuters.
